classification.difficultyReason: Convert the expression to a single sinusoid and use its phase and amplitude to place zeros, extrema and endpoints on the restricted graph.

answer.short:
$y=2\sin\left(x+\frac{2\pi}3\right)$.

Amplitude $2$; dilate $y=\sin x$ vertically by a factor of $2$ and translate it left by $\frac{2\pi}3$. The graph is shown below.
answer.worked:
Use the sine-sum form and equate coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}\sqrt3\cos x-\sin x&=R(\sin x\cos\alpha+\cos x\sin\alpha)\\R\sin\alpha&=\sqrt3\\R\cos\alpha&=-1\\R&=\sqrt{(\sqrt3)^2+(-1)^2}=2\\\tan\alpha&=-\sqrt3\end{align*}$$
Since $\sin\alpha>0$ and $\cos\alpha<0$, $\alpha$ is in the second quadrant.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\frac{2\pi}3\\\sqrt3\cos x-\sin x&=2\sin\left(x+\frac{2\pi}3\right)\end{align*}$$
Dilate $y=\sin x$ vertically by a factor of $2$ and translate it left by $\frac{2\pi}3$. The period remains $2\pi$.
The endpoints are $(0,\sqrt3)$ and $(2\pi,\sqrt3)$. The zeros are at $x=\frac\pi3,\frac{4\pi}3$, the minimum is $\left(\frac{5\pi}6,-2\right)$, and the maximum is $\left(\frac{11\pi}6,2\right)$.
